messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on private-vpc inference-gateway cluster 'gw-prod-eu' (eu-west-1). 5xx rate 18% over 5m, latency p99 spike. Affected tenant(s): fitlytics-prod (private deployment). Paging on-call: @sre-oncall-1. Metrics: https://console.redwood/alerts/2712348901
sre-oncall-1: Ack, i'm on it. switching to this thread. Can someone confirm customer impact (which endpoints, how many requests failing)?
cs-carly: Fitlytics CS here — they're seeing many 504s from their private endpoints (pvt-1234). Reported since ~09:03 UTC, affecting inference calls for a subset of users. They're high priority; opening ticket on their side.
sre-oncall-1: Looking at gateway logs now — tons of upstream reset / connection reset by peer lines. Pulling netstats and conntrack from nat gateways.
eng-runtime-amy: I see backend retransmits and TLS handshake failures to model-servers via peering link. Something's dropping or asymmetrically routing packets.
# logs (tail from gateway):
```
2026-03-15T09:06:12Z gw-prod-eu[proxy]: upstream reset by peer id=fitlytics/pvt-1234 conn=0x7f3c2a
2026-03-15T09:06:14Z gw-prod-eu[proxy]: 504 upstream read timeout id=fitlytics/pvt-1234
2026-03-15T09:07:01Z gw-prod-eu[proxy]: connection reset by peer (errno=104) src=10.2.5.12:443 dst=10.2.1.33:56784
```

ben-netops: Ran conntrack checks on nat-gw-az2 — conntrack_count=64512 / conntrack_max=65536. Ephemeral port usage is very high. Also noticed BGP withdraws on peering session vpc-pe-12 -> peer-asn 64512, intermittent every ~30s. Could be combined: conntrack exhaustion + peering flaps => asymmetric replies and resets.
sre-oncall-1: If conntrack is that high we can either increase limits or add another NAT/egress appliance. Which is fastest?
ben-netops: Fastest is scale NAT autoscaling group and temporarily reroute affected customer's route to spare public-egress. I'll trigger scale + open vendor ticket for BGP flaps.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_group nat-eu-prod desired=4 current=3 -> launching instance i-0abc1234efgh5678
eng-runtime-amy: I can add a temporary route for fitlytics pvt-1234 to nat-gw-spare in eu-west-1. That will exercise a different egress path and avoid the flapping peering.
sre-oncall-1: Do it. Post the route change command you run so we can revert after.
ben-netops: Route add command (aws CLI example):
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-pvt-1234-eu --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-gw-spare-0abcd
```
Note: replace with internal infra-tooling if using orchestration.
eng-runtime-amy: Applying route change now for rtb-pvt-1234-eu -> nat-gw-spare-0abcd.
sre-oncall-1: Running curl from test-host (in same private vpc) to a fitlytics inference endpoint to validate:
```
curl -v --max-time 10 https://pvt-1234.fitlytics.private.redwood/v1/infer | jq .status
```
Before change: 504/timeout. Immediately after route switch: 200 OK, response time ~420ms.
cs-carly: Fitlytics CS confirms partial recovery: majority of requests now succeed, they still see occasional 5xx while we verify. Thanks.
ben-netops: Conntrack dropped to ~24500 after additional nat instance warmed up and reroute. BGP withdraws still visible but traffic not hitting affected path now. Opening vendor ticket: TKT-2026-558 to cloud-peering-team — attaching bgp logs.
ops-manager-lee: Good mitigation. Carly please prepare customer-facing update: what happened, what we changed, ETA for full remediation.
cs-carly: Draft: "We identified elevated error rates caused by a combination of ephemeral port exhaustion on our NAT egress and intermittent peering route flaps. We have temporarily rerouted your traffic to an alternative egress which has reduced 5xxs. Our network team is working with the cloud vendor to resolve the peering flaps; ETA initial fix 2-4 hours; we will follow up with a post-incident report." Sending now.
sre-oncall-1: Next steps for us: 1) Keep reroute in place for pvt-1234 until the peering session is stable. 2) Increase conntrack_max and reduce conntrack timeout on nat gateways as a short-term safety valve. 3) Work with cloud vendor to resolve BGP flaps and confirm AS path stability. 4) Postmortem with root cause and mitigation (rate-limits, better autoscale, circuit fallback).
ben-netops: I've set conntrack_max=131072 on nat-gw instances and lowered timeout to 60s as temporary. Monitoring.
intra-bot: monitor: alert_suppression applied for next 30m for gw-prod-eu to avoid noisy alerts during mitigation window.
sre-oncall-1: Metrics now: 5xx rate down from 18% -> 2.3% over last 5m for gw-prod-eu. p99 latency trending down but we'll watch. Marking as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
ops-manager-lee: Great. Keep this thread updated with vendor ticket ID and time of full revert. We'll schedule postmortem after incident.
cs-carly: Customer updated and acknowledged, says they can operate with the temporary routing. Will escalate if anything else.
sre-oncall-1: I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand to eng-runtime for cleanup and postmortem. Thanks team.
incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated by @sre-oncall-1 at 2712349015. If metrics regress, paging will resume.
